card.name: Words setting up a sequence of steps
card.fires_on: Small connecting words (has, have, then, by) and nearby nouns in dosing instructions where a condition or earlier step is about to be stated as done, such as 'has been established' or 'followed by'.

modes.label: Auxiliary before 'been'
modes.description: The verb has or have right before a past-participle such as been established or been measured, setting a prerequisite.
modes.example: serum testosterone concentrations<< have>> been measured in the morning on at least

modes.label: Next-step linkers
modes.description: Words like then or by that lead into the following step or dose in a schedule.
modes.example: Administer 48 mg,<< then>> resume the planned treatment schedule.

modes.label: Condition on a patient
modes.description: Words in a 'only after a patient has failed' type clause.
modes.example: only after a<< patient>> has failed to achieve the desired effect with

card.writes: It pushes toward words of repetition or continuity and away from words meaning 'afterward', so it adds little clear sequencing content.
card.plain: It lights up on small words in dosing directions that lead into a step order or a requirement that must be met first.
